items.title: Alpha School's AI-tutored students: only 42% hit the 2x learning goal
items.summary: Internal data reported by the NYT shows about half of Alpha School's K-8 private-campus students missed the math target, and students who started behind did worse. The school charges $75K tuition and promises students learn twice as fast with AI-led instruction.
items.whyItMatters: A sober data point that AI tutoring alone doesn't guarantee faster learning, which argues for measurable progress tracking and human-style accountability in the Romain/Anna tutor.

items.title: LangChain raises $300M at $3B valuation; LangSmith claims 7,000 customers
items.summary: LangChain's Series C was led by CapitalG and more than doubles its valuation from a year ago. Its LangSmith product for building and managing agents is used by Nvidia, Toyota and Salesforce.
items.whyItMatters: Signals that agent tooling and observability are maturing, which is useful if the tutor needs tracing or evals for its voice agents.
